_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For runzero the manifest gained: RUNZERO_BASE_URL. server.json gained: RUNZERO_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: RUNZERO_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: org bulk-remove-custom-integration (POST /org/custom-integrations/{custom_integration_id}/bulk/remove). runzero 4.34.2 reprint (create-alias-only-on-create): press 4.34.2 no longer aliases bulk-remove-custom-integration but gives `create` to org clear-bulk-asset-owners (`clear` is not in its action-verb list), so `org create` removed the owners of every asset a search matched. tools/apply_edits.py drops the alias from every generated command whose name is not create-shaped (a class rule); TestOnlyCreateShapedCommandsAnswerToCreate walks the whole tree. Test seen failing first: seen/create-alias-only-on-create-seen-failing.log in the run dir.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: org create-sample and org create-scan take the explorer (agent) ID as --agent-id instead of a local --agent, so --agent is the agent-mode switch on every command; the body still carries its agent field
handfixes.why: A command-local flag that takes a value, registered under the name of a persistent root switch, replaces that switch on its command: Cobra keeps the command's own flag. Every SKILL, guide and MCP recipe tells an agent to add --agent for agent mode, so on this command a bare --agent stopped with 'flag needs an argument', and --agent followed by another flag swallowed that flag as its value (halopsa `tickets list --agent --dry-run` sent the live request: the --dry-run became the agent filter). The press does not reserve the root flag names when it names spec parameters (internal/generator/flag_collision.go reserves only its own --all/--wait/--stdin), so a reprint re-emits the shadow. tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py now fails any value-taking local flag over a persistent switch.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: reserve the root persistent flag names (agent, json, dry-run, quiet, ...) in reservedFlagNamesForEndpoint so a spec parameter of the same name gets a distinct public flag; until then, keep the rename here.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name, and no file stores operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds; applied by tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py. The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. An operator-named write that repeats a credential the program holds is withheld by the shared credential kit (credkit-wiring): profiles.json, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl and feedback.jsonl pass its file sinks, and the learn tables (learnings, playbooks, candidates, recall misses, entity aliases, patterns) its SQLite driver. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments (the credential kit withholds stored text that repeats a held credential).

handfixes.summary: spec.yaml declares x-pp-pagination none on the six GETs whose page_size switches the response to a {<entity>: [...], next_key} page (assets, services, wireless, software, vulnerabilities exports and /account/events.json), so sync asks without page_size and receives the whole export as the documented bare array
handfixes.why: The vendor's own spec (AssetExportResponse and siblings) documents both shapes; press 4.34.2 (and 4.24) recognize neither start_key nor next_key, so sync sent page_size=100, took page one and stopped: a sync of an org with more than 100 assets, services or findings silently kept the first 100. Spec-encoded (tools/spec_fix.py): survives every reprint from this spec. TestDefaultSyncTakesWholeExports asserts no export request carries page_size or start_key. (runzero 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own holder, output chokepoint, secret funnel, persistence gates and decoders. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; every API, streaming, feedback, deliver and probe client goes through credkit.Transport (client.OutboundGuard, the origin pin of api-origin-pinned on top); every file write except the connector's own 0600 credential store and config file goes through the kit; every store opens through internal/credsql (credkit.SQLDriver); the MCP stdio and HTTP servers pass credkit.MCPIn, MCPOut, MCPHTTP and MCPTools; child processes run through credkit.RunCommand. Response credential fields (an API key's token, export and download tokens, an access token, a client secret) are masked by name as "[credential withheld]" in the one answer every sink is fed from, so the rest of the record prints.
handfixes.why: Each connector-only check closed one shape and the next review found the next shape (an encoding, a split delivery, an 8-character piece, a mask-shaped value, a form-encoded body). The kit holds every part of every declared credential at startup and as responses arrive, and checks every sink, so the shape stops mattering, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. Holder-incomplete (Codex round 2 on the 4.34.2 reprint): runZero answered an error as an x-www-form-urlencoded body whose token field held a URL-shaped credential; TestHolderIncompleteFormBodyTokenNeverPrinted runs it on the built binary, seen failing on the pre-kit build (pub-review/seen/holder-incomplete-seen-failing.log) and passing through the kit (ResponseFields token). A reprint rewrites the generated sinks and mains: these asserts make that fail instead of silently dropping the routing.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring (mains, transports, file sinks, SQLite driver, MCP servers) and the Declarations literal.

The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).
